claims.claim: PR #1052 does NOT implement automatic re-subscription inside the library; it only emits a synthetic Event::Reconnect after subsequent successful CONNACKs, and the application must re-subscribe in the poll() loop when it sees that event.
claims.stance_target: Even if merged, rumqttc would still require application-side re-subscription logic — the library does not remember or replay subscriptions itself
claims.scope_conditions: PR #1052 description; rumqttc v5 module scope, with v4 left as follow-up
claims.quoted_support: rumqttc itself doesn't remember them either, so the application is silent on the new session until it re-subscribes — but it has no signal that a reconnect happened. ... the caller pattern is: Ok(Event::Reconnect) => { for (topic, qos) in &my_subs { client.subscribe(topic, *qos).await?; } }

claims.claim: PR #1052's problem statement confirms the core footgun for the ha-linux-agent use case: after a transport drop and reconnect with clean_session = true, every subscription is gone on the broker and the client process keeps running with no error and no incoming publishes — 'a long-standing rumqttc footgun'.
claims.stance_target: A fleet agent built on rumqttc 0.24.0 with clean_session=true will silently lose all MQTT subscriptions after any reconnect unless it explicitly re-subscribes
claims.scope_conditions: rumqttc behaviour with clean_session=true or v5 session expiry; issue #250
claims.quoted_support: After a transport drop and successful reconnect, the broker has a fresh session. With clean_session = true (or session expiry), every subscription the client had is gone. rumqttc itself doesn't remember them either, so the application is silent on the new session until it re-subscribes — but it has no signal that a reconnect happened. This is #250: a long-standing rumqttc footgun where a transient network blip leaves a process running but unable to receive any publishes, with no error in the event loop (the connection is "fine" again, just empty of subscriptions).
